name: Misket sample: Remote work and wellbeing

codes.name: Boundaries
codes.description: Where work starts and stops, in time, space or attention.

children.name: Time
children.description: Work bleeding into evenings, weekends or otherwise blurring the workday's edges.

children.name: Space
children.description: A physical place (or the lack of one) that marks 'at work' versus 'at home'.

children.name: Notifications
children.description: Pings, messages and alerts that reach across the boundary uninvited.

codes.name: Connection
codes.description: How people stay (or fail to stay) socially linked to their team.

children.name: Isolation
children.description: Feeling cut off, lonely, or short on ordinary human contact.

children.name: Team rituals
children.description: Recurring practices — coffee chats, check-ins, offsites — that manufacture connection on purpose.

codes.name: Autonomy
codes.description: Control over how, when and where the work gets done.

children.name: Flexibility
children.description: Choosing one's own hours, pace or working pattern.

children.name: Trust
children.description: Being judged on output rather than visible presence, or the lack of that trust.

memos.title: About this sample
memos.body: This is a synthetic project so you can try Misket without importing your own data first. Three fictional interviews explore a made-up study, 'Remote work and wellbeing', with a small codebook, about two dozen pre-coded excerpts, two descriptor fields (Role, Years remote) and this memo. Delete it, recode it, or just poke around — nothing here is real research.

memos.title: Coding note
memos.body: Boundaries covers where the workday visibly starts or stops: a closed door, a shut laptop, a notification arriving off-hours. It is distinct from Autonomy, which is about who decides those hours, not where the line falls.
